stories.title: 'Moonies' church leader jailed for two years over bribery offences
stories.summary: The leader of the controversial Unification Church has been sentenced to two years in prison for bribing South Korea's former first lady and other political funding offences. A court found that Han Hak-ja's church gave Kim Keon Hee, the wife of ousted president Yoon Suk Yeol, two Chanel bags and a diamond necklace, together worth 80 million won ($57,900; £42,500). Earlier this year, Kim was sentenced to 20 months in jail for accepting bribes from the church. Han, the 83-year-old widow of the Unification Church's founder Sun Myung Moon, had repeatedly denied the allegations, calling them "false". A special counsel team appointed to the case said Kim received the luxury products from the church between April and July 2022, in exchange for business and political favours. The prosecutors said the probe was the first time the authorities have confirmed the church's attempt at buying influence in politics, and released photos of $19m (£14m) worth of cash found in Han's personal safe. South Korea's former first lady admitted to receiving Chanel bags, but said she later returned them without using them. Kim made a public apology when she appeared for questioning last August: "I am truly sorry that a nobody like me has caused concern to the people." The Unification Church, known formally as The Family Federation for World Peace and Unification, was founded in South Korea in the 1950s by Sun Myung Moon, who proclaimed himself the messiah. The church is probably best known for the mass weddings where thousands of couples were married by Han and her late husband and founder Sun Myung Moon in a stadium. Critics have described the group as "cult-like". Lawyers have accused it of coercing devotees, known colloquially as "Moonies" after its founder, to donate large sums of money.

stories.title: Outgoing defense minister expresses 'mixed' feelings following Cabinet reshuffle
stories.summary: SEOUL, Aug. 31 (Yonhap) -- Outgoing Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back expressed Mond...
article_sentences: Outgoing Defense Minister Ahn Gyu-back expressed Monday his "mixed" feelings about his more than yearlong tenure as the country's first civilian defense chief, as he is stepping down following a Cabinet reshuffle.

Ahn, a five-term veteran lawmaker in the liberal bloc, was named defense minister weeks after President Lee Jae Myung took office in June last year, becoming the country's first defense chief with a civilian background in over six decades.
Cheong Wa Dae announced Sunday that Lee nominated retired Army Gen.
Kang Shin-chul, former deputy commander of the South Korea-U.S. Combined Forces Command, as new defense minister.
"As the first civilian defense minister, I think I have both my share of achievements and shortcomings," Ahn told lawmakers at the National Assembly.
"I truly feel heavyhearted, and I can hardly hold back how I feel," he said.

Since assuming his post, Ahn has spearheaded a string of high-stakes and politically sensitive tasks, including Seoul's push to retake wartime operational control from the United States and its drive for merging three military academies into a single institution.
Notably, Ahn has recently faced strong pushback over the military academy consolidation plan, along with the scrutiny over his obscure position on his military service records.
Ahn has been under scrutiny after renewed allegations that he went absent without leave and served time in a military detention facility during his conscription period in the early 1980s.
The service period for a short-term conscript that Ahn had served at the time was 14 months, but Ahn served a total of 22 months.
Civic groups and the opposition party have questioned the eight-month discrepancy, a claim Ahn has denied as groundless, saying it was an administrative error.
Ahn has said he was called back after the initial discharge in early 1985 to complete roughly a month of makeup service over an investigation into a minor issue.

stories.title: Russian central bank buys yuan worth $69.5 mln with Aug 28 settlement
stories.summary: The volume of foreign currency purchases on the domestic market with settlement on August 27 amounted to $68.3 mln
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 31.
The Bank of Russia purchased yuan worth 6 bln rubles ($69.5 mln) on the domestic market with settlement on August 28, 2026, according to data published on the regulator’s website.
The volume of foreign currency purchases on the domestic market with settlement on August 27 amounted to 5.9 bln rubles ($68.3 mln).
The Bank of Russia conducts foreign currency purchase and sale operations on the domestic market in the yuan-ruble instrument in the currency section of the Moscow Exchange.

stories.title: Falklands’ oil industry, Rockhopper plans equity raise for second FPSO
stories.summary: Rockhopper Exploration is planning an equity capital raising to fund its share of a second FPSO, (OSX-1), for the Sea Lion oil field development in the Falkland Islands, since operator Navitas Petroleum exercised its option to acquire the vessel for some US$ 125 million with the purpose of further adding production to 125.000 barrels of oil per day.
article_sentences: Rockhopper Exploration is planning an equity capital raising to fund its share of a second FPSO, (OSX-1), for the Sea Lion oil field development in the Falkland Islands, since operator Navitas Petroleum exercised its option to acquire the vessel for some US$ 125 million with the purpose of further adding production to 125.000 barrels of oil per day.

According to information from oil and gas industry international agencies, Navitas will initially fund 100% of the OSX-1, while partners determine how she will be incorporated to the increased Sea Lion project.

Rockhopper that is a non-operating partner of the development with a 35% share and Sea Lion license-holder, announced that it will require extra funding to acquire its percentage rata interest in the FPSO and other expenditures.

Rockhopper affirmed that “Navitas has provided an update that it has (through a subsidiary) exercised an option to acquire the second FPSO, named the OSX-1, and the completion of the acquisition is expected during the coming month.”
The asset carries an aggregate cost of US$125 million and will target the so-called central development area, CDA, of the Sea Lion field.

Samuel Moody, Chief Executive Officer of Rockhopper, commented: 'Today’s update from Navitas reflects its continued commitment to developing and accelerating Sea Lion, and the consequential significant enhancement of the Project’s value.
We are working alongside Navitas to ascertain the optimal structure for Sea Lion’s participation in OSX-1 and are planning a Capital Raising to secure the required financing.
We have already received positive indications of support for this financing and we look forward to updating the market in due course as appropriate.'
The first phase of Sea Lion is underway, with drilling work scheduled to start in early 2027 in the so-called northern development area, with first oil expected in 1Q28.
Meantime the FPSO vessel Aoka Mizu, with 55,000b/d capacity, is on route to a shipyard in Asia where upgrading work will be carried out.
Onshore work is also underway in the Falkland Islands, targeting quay and shore-based components.
Navitas intends to use OSX-1 to accelerate development of the CDA, with 20 wells planned for CDA Phase 1 and another 18 for Phase 2.
